Augment an mvgam object's training data with fitted values and residuals

Source: R/tidier_methods.R
augment.mvgam.Rd

The training data with posterior summaries of the fitted value and residual of each row, under broom's column names.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
augment(
  x,
  robust = FALSE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  resp = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam object.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

conf.int

Logical. TRUE (the default) adds the credible interval columns .lower, .upper, .resid.lower and .resid.upper.

conf.level

Numeric. Probability covered by the credible interval reported in conf.low / conf.high. Defaults to 0.95.

resp

Character specifying which response variable for multivariate models. NULL (default) returns predictions for all responses.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

Value

A tibble (or list, when class(x$data) == "list") with the original training data plus:

  • .observed -- the response value.

  • .fitted -- the posterior mean (or median) fitted value.

  • .se.fit -- the posterior standard deviation (or MAD) of the fitted value.

  • .lower, .upper -- the lower / upper bound of the conf.level credible interval for .fitted. Present only when conf.int = TRUE.

  • .resid -- the posterior mean (or median) residual.

  • .resid.se -- the posterior standard deviation (or MAD) of the residual.

  • .resid.lower, .resid.upper -- the residual credible interval bounds. Present only when conf.int = TRUE.

  • .unit -- only for closure-unit families (nmix(), occ()): the closure-unit ID this row belongs to. Rows sharing the same .unit share the same .resid* columns (see below).

Closure-unit families (nmix(), occ())

.fitted is the expected count of each visit: psi * p for occ() and lambda * p for nmix(). residuals.mvgam() computes one residual per closure unit, a site in a season, from the PIT of the summed visit counts. Each visit row of a unit repeats that residual. The .unit column names the unit.

See also

fitted.mvgam(), residuals.mvgam()

Other tidiers: glance.mvgam(), tidy.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The training data with fitted values and residuals appended
aug <- augment(mod)
head(aug)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 13
#>       y series    time      x .observed .fitted .se.fit .lower .upper   .resid
#>   <int> <fct>    <int>  <dbl>     <int>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1     2 series_1     1  0.841         2    1.97   0.833  0.756   3.99  0.207  
#> 2    14 series_1     2 -1.02         14   13.3    3.10   7.95   20.0   0.295  
#> 3     6 series_1     3 -0.441         6    5.84   1.80   2.86   10.2   0.202  
#> 4     1 series_1     4 -1.63          1    4.23   1.48   1.91    7.61 -1.66   
#> 5     5 series_1     5  1.85          5    3.82   1.40   1.70    6.96  0.730  
#> 6     5 series_1     6 -1.96          5    5.38   1.84   2.48    9.69 -0.00750
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: .resid.se <dbl>, .resid.lower <dbl>, .resid.upper <dbl>

# Residuals against fitted values, from one tibble
plot(aug$.fitted, aug$.resid, xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual")
